name: 10th and Sheridan (opened as Sheridan on 10th)
headline: WellPower (the Mental Health Center of Denver) built Sheridan on 10th, a three-story, 60-unit permanent supportive housing building for chronically homeless adults at 30% AMI in Denver's Villa Park neighborhood, with a 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA; it opened on 2025-06-24.
why_it_matters: It is a completed, repeatable model of a behavioral health provider developing its own 9% supportive housing: trauma-informed design, Division of Housing vouchers on every unit, a forgivable $3.1M Denver linkage-fee loan, a Denver Housing Authority partnership for tax exemption, and an infrastructure cost share with neighboring landowners.

status.label: Open: grand opening 2025-06-24
status.detail: Groundbreaking was in spring 2024 (Mile High CRE reported it on 2024-05-20) and WellPower held a ribbon-tying grand opening on 2025-06-24; WellPower's property page says "Now Open". Occupancy level and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not public.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and any WellPower or Denver HOST report on occupancy and housing retention.

background.text: WellPower's second 9% supportive housing project after Sanderson Apartments (60 units, 2017, part of Denver's Social Impact Bond); WellPower said Sheridan on 10th reuses lessons from Sanderson, such as the L-shaped plan for sightlines from reception to every entrance.

In August 2021 the city asked the four adjoining landowners to make an extension of W. 11th Avenue the primary site access; the owners agreed to a Drainage and Road Cost Share Agreement covering $1,581,401 of road extension and water detention costs, split among the four.

Entitlements were administrative: the Site Development Plan was submitted in September 2022, with approval tied to transportation engineering plans for the 11th Avenue extension and 10th Avenue sidewalks.

Denver's loan was approved by the Safety, Housing, Education & Homelessness Committee on 2024-03-20 and adopted by City Council on 2024-06-03; the agreement requires completion within 24 months and records a 60-year covenant.
The loan agreement records the City's approval of WellPower's planned merger with Jefferson Center for Mental Health, then expected on 2024-07-01.
Market study figures in the application: 12.4% capture rate; lease-up of 30 units a month, stabilized in about two months.
